Metadata.title: Manar Trading — Fresh Red Sea & Gulf Seafood in Saudi Arabia
Metadata.description: Manar Trading supplies fresh Red Sea and Arabian Gulf fish to homes, restaurants and hotels across Saudi Arabia. Landed daily, iced within minutes, delivered same day.
Metadata.ogTitle: Manar Trading — Fresh Seafood, Saudi Arabia
Metadata.ogDescription: Red Sea and Arabian Gulf fish, landed daily and delivered same day across the Kingdom.

Nav.cutoff: Landed today · same-day delivery — message us for today's cutoff

Hero.subtitle: With Manar Trading, you get fresh seafood to start your day right, fuel your business, and bring your family together at the table — every single day.

Fork.title: Buying for a table, or for a kitchen?
Fork.copy: They are not the same order, and this site has stopped pretending they are. Pick the one that is you — the rest of the page follows it.

table.title: Buying for the table
table.copy: One box, this week, for your own kitchen. Pick the fish, say how you want it cut, and we quote it by the kilo before anything is prepared.
table.p1: Order by the piece or by the kilo, for one meal or a week
table.p2: Cleaned, scaled and cut how you cook it, at no charge
table.p3: Quoted and confirmed on WhatsApp before we cut

kitchen.title: Buying for a kitchen
kitchen.copy: A standing list, a delivery window you can build a service around, and one person who knows what your kitchen takes. Restaurants, hotels and caterers.
kitchen.p1: A fixed daily or weekly list, agreed once
kitchen.p2: The same delivery window every day
kitchen.p3: One contact who knows your kitchen, not a call centre

Offerings.title: What the counter carries
Offerings.copy: Three ways in: the fish counter, the shellfish season, and a standing order for a kitchen.
Offerings.caveat: This is the range we carry, not a live landing report. What is actually on ice on any given morning depends on the boats, the weather and the season — message us and we will tell you what is there today.

fish.title: Fish
fish.copy: Hamour, Kanad, Shaour, Najil, Sea Bass and Sea Bream — landed on the Red Sea and Gulf coasts, or flown in overnight.

shellfish.title: Crustaceans & seafood
shellfish.copy: Gulf shrimp head-on and still snapping, crayfish, lobster, crab, octopus and squid — sold on the day they land.

orders.title: Standing kitchen orders
orders.copy: A fixed list, the same delivery window every day, and one contact who knows your kitchen.

Seas.title: A country with two very different seas
Seas.copy: Reef species off the Red Sea shelves, pelagics from the offshore fleet, and Gulf shellfish inside their licensed seasons. The counter never looks the same two weeks running.

red.name: Red Sea
red.copy: Warm, deep and reef-built. This is where the fish the Saudi table asks for by name comes from — Hamour off the Farasan Banks, Shaour and Najil from the southern shelves.
red.ports: Jeddah · Yanbu · Al Lith · Qunfudhah · Jazan · Farasan
red.season: Fishes year-round; the reef species peak October to March.

gulf.name: Arabian Gulf
gulf.copy: Shallower, silted, and far more seasonal. The Gulf is where the shrimp season is set by licence, and where the Kanad this whole country grills comes off the boats.
gulf.season: Shrimp only inside the licensed season, which is set fresh each year.

imported.label: The third water
imported.copy: Farmed bream and bass, North Atlantic lobster, Nile perch — imported, and labelled as imported.

Range.title: Everything we carry, named
Range.copy: Two headings on the spec sheet. Every line is quoted by the kilo at the time of the order, against that morning's landing — which is why there is no price printed anywhere on this site.

source.title: We source
source.copy: Our own buyers take the fish straight off the boats on the Red Sea and Gulf coasts, and we import the rest ourselves — never through a wholesaler, never a second day.

choose.title: You choose
choose.copy: Pick your species and tell us how you cook it — whole, butterflied, steaked or filleted. Cut to order just before dispatch, at no extra charge.

deliver.title: We deliver
deliver.copy: Buried in flake ice minutes after landing and held at 0 – 2 °C to your door, with same-day delivery across the Kingdom.

Cuts.title: Tell us how you cook it
Cuts.copy: The second question at any counter, and the one most sites never ask. Every line we carry can be prepared five ways, cut to order just before dispatch.
Cuts.note: None of this costs extra, and nothing is cut in advance. Say which one you want in the order notes or on WhatsApp — and if you are not sure, tell us the dish and we will pick for you.

whole.title: Whole
whole.copy: As it came off the boat, head and tail on. The way it is bought at the quay.

cleaned.title: Cleaned
cleaned.copy: Scaled, gutted and gilled, ready for the oven or the charcoal.

steaked.title: Steaked
steaked.copy: Cross-cut through the bone into even steaks. Holds together on a grill.

filleted.title: Filleted
filleted.copy: Both sides off the frame, skin on or skinless, pin bones out.

butterflied.title: Butterflied
butterflied.copy: Opened along the spine and laid flat — the cut for a whole grilled fish.

delivery.q: Where do you deliver, and by when?
delivery.a: Same-day delivery across the Kingdom on chilled transport, with the cut-off depending on where you are. Message us with your city and we will give you today's cut-off and window before you order — better that than a time printed here that is wrong for your street.

weight.q: How do you charge when the fish weighs more or less than I ordered?
weight.a: You are invoiced on the actual weight at packing, never the estimate. If a whole fish comes in over what you asked for, we call you before it leaves the counter and you decide.

cuts.q: Can I choose how the fish is cleaned and cut?
cuts.a: Yes, and it costs nothing. Whole, cleaned, cross-cut steaks, skin-on or skinless fillets, butterflied — tell us in the order notes. Everything is prepared right before dispatch, never in advance.

trade.q: Do you supply restaurants and hotels?
trade.a: Yes — it is one of the two ways we sell, and it works differently from a household order: a standing list, a fixed delivery window, and one contact who knows your kitchen. Minimums and terms are set per kitchen, so talk to us and we will build it around your service.

problem.q: What happens if I am not happy with the fish?
problem.a: Tell us on the day it arrives and we will make it right — refunded, or replaced on the next run. No photographs, no forms, no argument.

payment.a: The order is quoted and confirmed on WhatsApp and payment is arranged there — the site does not take card payments yet. Ask what we can accept for your order and we will tell you straight.

faq.title: What people ask before the first order
faq.copy: Answered plainly. Where something is not settled yet, this says so rather than inventing a figure.

close.title: Eat it tonight.
close.copy: Tell us the species, the weight and how you want it cut. We confirm the quote and the delivery window on WhatsApp, and nothing is cut until you say yes.
close.note: Not sure what to ask for?

Shop.title: Everything on the ice today
Shop.copy: Two headings, five ways of cutting them, three waters. Availability moves with the boats, so the list is rebuilt as the fish lands — and every line is quoted by the kilo when you order.

empty.title: Nothing matches that
empty.copy: Try another heading, another water, or a different cut. The counter carries sixteen lines in all — clearing the filters shows every one of them.

Shop.note: Cut to order, free of charge, right before dispatch — never in advance. If a line will not take the cut you want, it does not appear under that filter.

prep.a: Tell us in the order notes — whole, cleaned, steaked, filleted or butterflied. Preparation is free and done right before dispatch, never in advance.

size.q: What if the size I want is gone?
size.a: We call you before dispatch with the nearest grade available and adjust the order by weight. You are never sent a size we could not supply.

trade.a: Yes, on a standing list with a fixed delivery window and one contact who knows your kitchen. Minimums and terms are set per kitchen, so talk to us and we will build it around your service.

priced.title: Priced on WhatsApp
priced.copy: Send us the grade, the weight and the cut. We confirm today's rate by the kilo and the delivery window before anything is prepared.

Product.message: Hello Manar Trading. I would like {qty} kg of {name} ({arabic}), {grade} grade ({weight}), prepared {cut}. Could you confirm the price and the delivery window?

chilled.title: 0 – 2 °C
chilled.copy: Iced at landing and held cold to your door

cutToOrder.title: Cut to order
cutToOrder.copy: Prepared before dispatch, never in advance

guarantee.title: Guaranteed
guarantee.copy: Not right on the day? Refunded or replaced

nutrition.note: Typical values per 100 g of raw edible portion.
nutrition.placeholder: These four figures are indicative, not measured on our own stock. Treat them as a guide and ask us if a number matters for your kitchen.

cooking.title: Best cooked as
cooking.copy: Season simply and let the fish carry the plate. If you tell us the dish when you order, we will cut it the way that dish wants.
cooking.s1: Take it out of the fridge fifteen minutes before cooking so it comes closer to room temperature.
cooking.s2: Pat the skin completely dry, then salt it generously — that is what gives you crisp skin.
cooking.s3: Cook it four-fifths of the time on the first side. Turn once, never twice.
cooking.s4: Rest it three minutes before serving. The centre finishes cooking off the heat.

hero.title: A seafood company that buys, grades and supplies
hero.copy: Manar Trading buys off the Red Sea and Arabian Gulf coasts and imports the rest, then grades every box before it leaves the building. One counter, two kinds of customer: kitchens that need the same standard on every delivery, and families buying dinner for tonight.

what.title: One chain, boat to counter
what.p1: Manar means lighthouse — the fixed point a boat steers towards. That is the whole idea behind the name: one supplier a kitchen can rely on, holding the same standard on every box that leaves us.
what.p2: We buy off both Saudi coasts and import the rest ourselves, so the list stays full even when a season closes. Nothing is accepted before it is graded, everything stays in the cold chain, and it is cut the way you asked for just before dispatch.
what.p3: We sell by the kilo to a family and by the crate to a kitchen. Both get the same fish, off the same ice, graded by the same standard.
what.caption: Stand-in photograph. Manar's own counter is on the shot list.

story.title: This is where the founder's story goes
story.p1: Every seafood company in this trade runs a founder's story on this page, and the good ones are specific: a name, a first boat, the year it started. We have not been given those details yet, so there is nothing written here pretending to be them.
story.p2: What can be said without inventing anybody is on the rest of this page — which waters the fish comes from, how it is graded, and what happens between the quay and your door. When the real account is recorded it lands here, in full.

r1.title: Honest about age
r1.copy: If a box came in yesterday, we say so when you ask. Day-two fish is sold as day-two fish or it is not sold.

r2.title: Seasons, to the day
r2.copy: A closed season is closed. Undersized fish is refused at the quay rather than graded down and quietly put on the counter.

r3.title: Graded before accepted
r3.copy: Nothing goes onto the ice before it has been looked at properly. What fails grading leaves on the truck it arrived on.

r4.title: Cut when you order
r4.copy: Scaling, gutting and portioning happen just before dispatch. Nothing is cut in advance to save a minute at the counter.

range.title: What the counter carries
range.note: These four figures are counted from the catalogue itself, so they cannot drift out of step with what is actually listed.

cta.title: The rest is easier said than written
cta.copy: Ring the counter or send a message. Where it came from, when it landed, how it was handled — those are the questions we like.

hero.title: Tell us what you need and when you need it
hero.copy: Orders, kitchen supply, quotes, or just a question about what is worth buying this week. Every path on this page ends with a person, not a ticket number.

call.label: Call the counter
call.note: The fastest answer during opening hours

whatsapp.label: WhatsApp
whatsapp.note: Send your list and we quote by the kilo

Contact.unconfirmed: The phone number is live. The email address, the opening hours and the CR number are still placeholders awaiting confirmation, so call before you travel.

paths.title: Which one is this?
paths.copy: The two conversations are genuinely different, so they start differently. Both open WhatsApp with the opening line already written.

table.title: Buying for the table
table.copy: One order, cut the way you cook it, delivered the same day. Tell us the fish and the weight, and we quote by the kilo before anything is packed.
table.message: Hello Manar. I would like to order for my home. Here is what I need:

kitchen.title: Buying for a kitchen
kitchen.copy: Restaurants, hotels and caterers. Standing orders, weekly lists, a grade you need held to every time. Terms are agreed per kitchen rather than off a published tier.
kitchen.message: Hello Manar. I am enquiring about supply for a kitchen. Here are the details:

form.title: Write the message, then send it yourself
form.copy: This fills in a WhatsApp message and hands it to your own phone. Nothing is submitted from this page and nothing is stored here — you press send, and the thread stays in your account.
form.messagePlaceholder: Six kilos of Grouper, cleaned and butterflied, Thursday morning to Al Rawdah…
form.errMessage: A little more detail helps us quote accurately
form.emailFallback: Not on WhatsApp? Send the same details to {email}.

hours.title: Opening hours
hours.note: The counter is fullest between 6 and 10 in the morning, straight after the boats unload.

faq.title: Questions we get every week
faq.copy: If yours is not here, call the counter — we would rather answer it properly than guess in writing.
